scored.name: Allswell
scored.subcategory: Mental Health — virtual therapy and group programs for the LGBTQ+ community
scored.founders: Dawn Androphy (co-founder and CEO) and Connor Gordon (co-founder and CTO). Techstars says they founded Allswell in 2024 and began building it at Stanford Graduate School of Business. Stanford reports that Androphy and Gordon had worked at Microsoft; Androphy studied for an MBA at Stanford and had a background in LGBTQ+ advocacy. Further background details for Gordon were not confirmed.
scored.description: Virtual behavioral health care for the LGBTQ+ community, including individual therapy, group programs, and trauma-informed care. The company says its services are covered by commercial insurance and Medicaid and matches patients with licensed therapists who are LGBTQ+ or screened for experience serving the community.
scored.evidence: Techstars reports hundreds of active patients and more than 1,500 billable sessions per month. It also reports company-provided outcomes: after 60 days of treatment, 77% of patients in its most recent cohorts showed improvement in anxiety and 71% showed improvement in depression. These are reported as company figures; independent clinical validation was not confirmed.

source_notes.supports: October 14, 2026 seed announcement and amount; total funding; product and insurance coverage; operating footprint; founders and founding context; patient, session, and company-reported outcome figures.
San Francisco headquarters; $7 million seed round; earlier $1.3 million pre-seed; hundreds of patients, approximately 40 clinicians, and insurance/Medicaid participation.
Androphy's Stanford MBA, LGBTQ+ advocacy background, prior work at Microsoft, and collaboration with co-founder Connor Gordon.
Company background and the founders' shared LGBTQ+ advocacy and volunteer work.
Company website.

news.title: Allswell Raises $7M Seed to Build the Behavioral Health Home for the LGBTQ+ Community - Techstars

scorecard.subcategory: Mental Health — virtual therapy and group programs for the LGBTQ+ community

segment_fit.rationale: Directly serves a population facing distinct behavioral-health access needs through therapy and group programs, fitting the thesis’s mental-health and equity priorities. The product is care delivery rather than merely a wellness label.

stage_and_terms_fit.rationale: A reported $7 million seed round is within the acceptable stage range, but valuation, instrument, ownership availability, and ability to accommodate a $25K–$50K check are unknown. U.S. headquarters is reported, but legal domicile and for-profit status are unconfirmed.

evidence_bar.rationale: Company-reported cohorts show 77% anxiety and 71% depression improvement after 60 days, but independent validation and study methods are not confirmed. The thesis requires evidence grounding for Wellness; these results are promising early signals, not verified clinical evidence.

revenue_path_independent_of_regulation.rationale: Unknown whether the business depends on regulatory clearance or has an alternative revenue path; the record says services are covered by commercial insurance and Medicaid but does not describe billing or regulatory exposure. No clearance-dependent product is described.

systems_adoption_and_paying_champion.rationale: Unknown whether there are payer or health-system partnerships, signed contracts, or a named paying champion. Reported insurance coverage and billable sessions do not establish payer contracting terms, reimbursement reliability, or repeatable adoption.

impact_and_health_equity.rationale: LGBTQ+ patients are the explicit target population, and matching with affirming or appropriately experienced licensed therapists plausibly addresses access and fit barriers. Company-reported patient outcomes are encouraging, but affordability, demographic reach, and independently measured impact remain unclear.

defensibility.rationale: Unknown whether the company has proprietary data, durable referral or payer relationships, or a trusted experience that is difficult to replicate. Therapy matching and virtual care alone may be readily copied.

founder_fit.rationale: Founders’ Microsoft backgrounds and the CEO’s LGBTQ+ advocacy are reported, but clinical, behavioral-health operating, or healthcare commercialization experience is not established. The record does not confirm clinical leadership or a medical advisory structure.

capex_light.rationale: Virtual therapy and group programs are services delivered by licensed therapists, with no owned clinical hardware or lab infrastructure described. The model appears relatively capex-light, though labor intensity and clinician economics are unknown.

scorecard.portfolio_conflict: None found; Allswell focuses on LGBTQ+ behavioral health, unlike Dopl Technologies’ remote diagnostic ultrasound.
scorecard.headline: Allswell is a mission-aligned LGBTQ+ virtual behavioral-health provider with encouraging but company-reported outcomes and unresolved questions about payer economics, clinical validation, and fund eligibility.
red_flags: Reported anxiety and depression improvements are company-provided; independent validation, cohort size, measurement instruments, and attrition are not confirmed.
Insurance coverage and billable-session volume do not establish contracted payer economics, collections, margins, or a sustainable clinician supply model.
Legal U.S. domicile and for-profit status are unconfirmed, despite reported U.S. headquarters.
The $7 million seed round may create a mismatch with the fund’s small check and ownership targets; valuation and round terms are unknown.
unknowns: Post-money valuation, security/instrument, round status, cap table, and available allocation.
Clinical outcomes methodology, independent evidence, clinical advisory structure, and safety protocols.
Payer contracts, reimbursement/collections, unit economics, therapist capacity, retention, and scalable acquisition channels.
diligence_questions: Can you share the study design behind the 60-day anxiety and depression improvement figures, including cohort sizes, instruments, comparison group, attrition, subgroup results, and any independent review or published evidence?

Which commercial insurers and Medicaid programs have executed contracts or authorized reimbursement, what are realized collections and contribution margins per session, and what evidence supports repeatable payer or provider adoption beyond reported billable volume?

What are the company’s legal domicile, for-profit status, current valuation and round terms, and the plan to scale affirming therapist supply and patient access while maintaining clinical quality and affordability?

scored.name: Cheiron (PhnyX Lab Inc.)
scored.subcategory: Biopharma R&D workflow / AI knowledge graph
scored.founders: Minseok Bae (CEO; studied computer science at Stanford before leaving to start the company), Harshit Gupta (CTO; computer science graduate studies at Stanford and undergraduate studies at IIT Bombay), and Jason Park (CPO; studied mathematics and computer science at Stanford and earned an MS in computer science).
scored.description: AI software for biopharma teams that connects biomedical, clinical, regulatory, patent, and commercial information to help organize and reason across a drug-development program. The company describes it as an AI-native operating system and knowledge graph for drug programs.

An earlier company announcement reported use by more than 60 companies, including all of South Korea’s top 10 pharmaceutical companies by revenue. These are company-reported adoption claims; I found no clinical-trial results or other evidence that Cheiron itself has demonstrated clinical efficacy.

news.title: AI biotech startup Cheiron launches $8 million seed round - The Korea News Plus

scorecard.subcategory: Biopharma R&D workflow / AI knowledge graph

segment_fit.rationale: Cheiron sells software to biopharma teams to organize drug-development programs, rather than delivering patient care or fitting one of the fund’s six defined healthcare segments. Its potential downstream effect on drug development is too indirect to establish thesis fit.

stage_and_terms_fit.rationale: The company is for-profit, U.S.-based, and at Seed stage, which fits several formal criteria. However, the announced $8 million round does not establish that a $25K–$50K check, 0.25%–1% ownership, or a post-money valuation at or below $10 million is available.

evidence_bar.rationale: The record cites company-reported professional adoption, but provides no independent validation of product performance or measurable health outcomes. No clinical evidence is reported, and the product’s claimed contribution to drug-development decisions is not quantified.

revenue_path_independent_of_regulation.rationale: The software may generate revenue without Cheiron obtaining regulatory clearance, but the record gives no pricing, revenue, or customer-contract details. The thesis’s specific requirement applies to products with meaningful regulatory risk; whether any Cheiron feature carries such risk is unknown.

systems_adoption_and_paying_champion.rationale: Use by major drug developers and more than 60 companies is reported by the company, but there is no evidence of paid pilots, contracts, named budget owners, or repeatable enterprise integration. The thesis’s health-system adoption standard is not directly applicable to this biopharma-facing product, and commercial validation remains unclear.

impact_and_health_equity.rationale: More efficient drug development could eventually benefit patients, but the record does not show that Cheiron improves access, affordability, clinical outcomes, or equity. A measurable and attributable impact pathway is unknown.

defensibility.rationale: The product combines information across biomedical, clinical, regulatory, patent, and commercial sources, but the record does not establish proprietary usage data, hard-to-replicate workflow adoption, or another durable moat. AI-based knowledge and workflow features may be vulnerable to competition or incumbent platforms.

founder_fit.rationale: The founders have computer science and mathematics backgrounds, but no healthcare practitioner, biopharma operator, clinical network, or relevant commercialization experience is provided. Their domain fluency and ability to reach purchasing decision-makers are unknown.

capex_light.rationale: The described product is AI software, with no owned laboratory, manufacturing, or hardware infrastructure identified. Operating costs and capital needs are not provided, so the capex-light assessment is provisional.

scorecard.portfolio_conflict: None found; Cheiron focuses on biopharma R&D software, while Dopl Technologies focuses on remote diagnostic ultrasound.
scorecard.headline: Cheiron has reported rapid adoption of biopharma workflow software, but it falls outside the fund’s six healthcare segments and has no demonstrated patient-impact or commercial evidence in the record.
red_flags: Outside the fund’s defined healthcare segments; any patient benefit is indirect and unproven.
Adoption figures are company-reported and do not establish paid, recurring enterprise use.
No measurable clinical, affordability, access, or health-equity outcomes are provided.
The $8 million Seed round does not establish fit with the fund’s valuation, ownership, or check-size limits.
unknowns: Post-money valuation, round terms, and availability of allocation for a small check.
Revenue, pricing, retention, customer concentration, and whether reported adoption is paid or active.
Independent product-performance evidence, customer references, and any measurable drug-development impact.
Founder experience in biopharma commercialization and the durability of data, workflow, or distribution advantages.
diligence_questions: What proportion of the reported users and company adopters are paying, retained customers, and can a customer provide evidence of measurable time or cost savings in a drug-development program?

What specific, attributable patient or public-health outcomes does Cheiron enable, and how would the company measure access, affordability, or equity impact within the fund’s five-to-seven-year horizon?

What are the round’s post-money valuation and terms, and what proprietary data, workflow integration, or other defensible advantage would protect the product from competing platforms or foundation-model providers?

scored.name: Accipiter Biosciences (Accipiter Bio)
scored.subcategory: Biopharma — computationally designed protein therapeutics for autoimmune disease and cancer
scored.round_date: July 21, 2026 (first sale reported in the SEC Form D; filing dated July 28, 2026)
scored.founders: Matthew Bick, Javier Castellanos, and Hector Rincon-Arano. Bick has a Ph.D. in Biophysics from The Rockefeller University and a B.S. in Microbiology from the University of Rochester, and worked at the University of Washington’s Institute for Protein Design. Castellanos is the company’s co-founder and CTO. GeekWire reports that Bick and two co-founders worked at Neoleukin; the source does not identify which two.
scored.description: Uses computational protein design to create de novo, multifunctional protein therapies intended to activate multiple cell-surface receptors or pathways at once, with an initial focus on autoimmune disease and cancer.
scored.evidence: The July 2026 seed extension was reported as approximately $10.5 million. The company has collaboration and license agreements with Pfizer and Kite Pharma; GeekWire reports an upfront payment and potential milestone payments and royalties for the Pfizer agreement. In November 2025, two company programs were preparing for pre-IND discussions with the FDA. I found no evidence that an Accipiter-developed therapy has entered a clinical trial. A GeekWire article mentions a Phase 1 candidate that underperformed, but identifies it as a Neoleukin candidate, not an Accipiter product.

source_notes.supports: Seattle location; $10.5 million seed extension; July 31, 2026 report date; seed-round classification; Pfizer and Kite agreements; team size; co-founders' Neoleukin background; clarification that the Phase 1 candidate discussed was not an Accipiter drug.
Form D details reported from the SEC filing: $10,492,778 sold, first sale July 21, 2026, filing July 28, 2026, Seattle principal place of business, and Delaware incorporation.
SEC EDGAR index for Accipiter Biosciences’ Form D filing dated July 28, 2026.
Washington registration describes the company as a Foreign Profit Corporation and gives its Seattle, Washington principal address and Delaware jurisdiction of incorporation.
Company description of its computationally designed, de novo multifunctional protein biologics and their intended multi-pathway activity.
Matthew Bick’s education and Institute for Protein Design background; Javier Castellanos’s role as co-founder and CTO.

Names the founders as Matthew J. Bick, Javier Castellanos, Hector Rincon, and Bill Arthur. This differs from other reporting; the three names listed above are the co-founders corroborated by additional sources.
Two programs preparing for pre-IND discussions as of November 2025; product approach and partnership details; distinguishes the underperforming Phase 1 candidate as a Neoleukin program.
Company-stated pipeline focus on autoimmunity and oncology.

news.title: Moving faster than planned, AI drug developer Accipiter Bio quietly tops up seed round with $10.5M - GeekWire

scorecard.subcategory: Biopharma — computationally designed protein therapeutics for autoimmune disease and cancer

segment_fit.rationale: Accipiter develops therapeutic proteins, placing it in Biopharma rather than the fund’s preferred capex-light Health Tech and Healthcare Services segments. Its potential health impact does not offset this explicit sector mismatch.

stage_and_terms_fit.rationale: The company is at Seed, within the acceptable stage range, but the reported round was approximately $10.5 million and the record gives no valuation, proposed fund terms, or evidence that a $25K–$50K check would secure the target ownership. Unknown whether the post-money valuation is within the $10M ceiling.

evidence_bar.rationale: No Accipiter-developed therapy is reported to have entered clinical trials; two programs were preparing for pre-IND discussions in November 2025. The cited underperforming Phase 1 candidate was a Neoleukin program, not Accipiter evidence.

revenue_path_independent_of_regulation.rationale: Pfizer and Kite agreements reportedly include licensing or collaboration economics, including an upfront payment and potential milestones and royalties for Pfizer. The record does not establish recurring or sufficiently credible revenue independent of regulatory progress and clinical success.

systems_adoption_and_paying_champion.rationale: The record identifies collaboration and license agreements with Pfizer and Kite, but does not describe a paying clinical champion, healthcare-system adoption, or a repeatable care-delivery implementation. Unknown how these partnerships translate into durable commercial validation.

impact_and_health_equity.rationale: Autoimmune disease and cancer are consequential areas, but the record provides no named target population, clinical outcome data, affordability or access plan, or health-equity strategy. Unknown whether the business and impact models reinforce one another.

defensibility.rationale: De novo, multifunctional protein design and agreements with Pfizer and Kite suggest potential technical and partnering advantages. The record does not establish proprietary-data advantages, validated therapeutic differentiation, or a durable competitive moat.

founder_fit.rationale: Co-founder Matthew Bick has a Ph.D. in Biophysics, protein-design experience at the University of Washington’s Institute for Protein Design, and prior Neoleukin experience among the founders. The record does not establish clinical-practitioner, healthcare commercialization, or women-founder alignment.

capex_light.rationale: The core business is therapeutic protein development, a Biopharma model with substantial research, manufacturing, and clinical-development needs. That conflicts with the fund’s preference for capex-light Health Tech and Healthcare Services.

scorecard.portfolio_conflict: No direct overlap found. Accipiter is a therapeutic protein developer, while Dopl Technologies focuses on robotics and AI for remote diagnostic ultrasound exams.
scorecard.headline: Accipiter has credible protein-design expertise and pharma partnerships, but its preclinical Biopharma model is outside the fund’s preferred segments and lacks demonstrated clinical evidence.
red_flags: Biopharma is a clear mismatch with the fund’s stated focus on capex-light Health Tech and Healthcare Services.
No Accipiter-developed therapy is reported to have entered clinical trials; programs were preparing for pre-IND discussions.
The reported $10.5 million Seed round is much larger than the fund’s typical check, and valuation and ownership terms are unknown.
The record does not establish a reliable revenue stream independent of regulatory and clinical progress.
unknowns: Post-money valuation, security terms, available allocation, and whether the round meets the fund’s ownership and return requirements.
Program-specific clinical rationale, safety and efficacy evidence, development costs, and timelines.
Economics, milestones, rights, and revenue recognized under the Pfizer and Kite agreements.
Affordability, target populations, access strategy, and measurable health-equity outcomes.
diligence_questions: What are the current valuation and proposed terms, and can a $25K–$50K investment achieve meaningful ownership within the fund’s $10M post-money ceiling?
What cash has been received under the Pfizer and Kite agreements, and what credible revenue can Accipiter generate if its programs face regulatory or clinical delays?
For each lead program, what preclinical evidence, development and manufacturing costs, and clinical milestones support a plausible path to patient impact within the fund’s seven-year impact horizon?

scored.name: ARTAN Bio
scored.founders: Michael Torres, Ph.D. (co-founder and chief scientific officer; previously co-founded and led CrossBridge Bio as CEO through its acquisition by Eli Lilly) and Anthony Schwartz, Ph.D. (co-founder; was CEO and transitioned to COO in July 2026). The sources found do not provide further education or career-background details for either founder.
scored.description: Develops an engineered suppressor-tRNA platform intended to recognize disease-causing nonsense mutations (premature stop codons) and restore production of full-length functional proteins. The company says the approach could apply to genetic and aging-related diseases.
scored.evidence: The company reported initial in-cell validation of its ARTAN-102 system and a preclinical animal-model signal across major organs, including the brain. The July 2026 financing was intended to support IND-enabling preclinical work and preparation for first-in-human development; the sources found do not establish human clinical evidence or trials.

source_notes.supports: Identifies ARTAN Bio as based in St. Petersburg, Florida; reports the $1 million seed round dated July 1, 2026, led by co-founder Michael Torres; describes Torres’s CrossBridge Bio background, leadership changes, product approach, and planned preclinical/IND-enabling work.

Reports an earlier $200,000 seed raise dated June 4, 2026; describes ARTAN-102 and the company’s reported initial in-cell validation; names Anthony Schwartz, Ph.D., as CEO and Michael Torres, Ph.D., as CSO at that time.
Company about page search result identifies Michael Torres, Ph.D., and reports a preclinical animal-model signal for ARTAN-102 across major organs, including the brain.
Identifies the startup referenced in the headline as ARTAN Bio and corroborates the $1 million seed round, St. Petersburg base, Michael Torres’s lead role, and the CEO/COO transition.

news.title: Eli Lilly acquisition payday fuels $1M seed round for St. Petersburg biotech startup - The Business Journals

segment_fit.rationale: ARTAN Bio is developing a therapeutic platform, not a Health Tech or Healthcare Services solution in the fund’s six focus segments. Its drug-development model also falls outside the thesis’s preference for capex-light opportunities.

stage_and_terms_fit.rationale: The reported Seed round is within the fund’s acceptable stage range, and the company is U.S.-based. The record does not establish for-profit status, valuation, security terms, or whether the fund’s target ownership and check size are feasible.

evidence_bar.rationale: Evidence is limited to company-reported in-cell validation and a preclinical animal-model signal; no human evidence or trials are established. A therapeutic platform intended to restore protein function faces a substantial clinical-validation burden.

revenue_path_independent_of_regulation.rationale: The seed financing is intended to fund IND-enabling work and preparation for first-in-human development. No services, licensing, or other commercial revenue path independent of regulatory progress is identified.

systems_adoption_and_paying_champion.rationale: The record provides no information about a health-system or payer champion, paid pilots, or adoption pathways. These criteria are not a natural fit for a preclinical therapeutic, and no alternative paying customer is identified.

impact_and_health_equity.rationale: Treating diseases caused by nonsense mutations could have meaningful health impact, but the target conditions, affected populations, access and affordability plan, and measurable outcomes are not established. The proposed aging-related applications are also not substantiated in the record.

defensibility.rationale: An engineered suppressor-tRNA platform could potentially support differentiation, but the record does not establish proprietary protection, freedom to operate, reproducibility, or a durable advantage. Evidence remains company-reported and preclinical.

founder_fit.rationale: Co-founder Michael Torres has a Ph.D. and previously led CrossBridge Bio through its acquisition by Eli Lilly, a relevant biotech commercialization signal. The record gives limited further background on either founder and does not establish the clinical or practitioner network emphasized in the thesis.

capex_light.rationale: Therapeutic development requiring IND-enabling studies and human trials is capital-intensive and exposed to long development timelines. No outsourced or otherwise capital-light development and revenue model is described.

scorecard.portfolio_conflict: None found; ARTAN Bio’s therapeutic platform does not directly overlap with Dopl Technologies’ remote diagnostic ultrasound business.
scorecard.headline: ARTAN Bio has experienced biotech leadership and early preclinical signals, but its capital-intensive, regulation-dependent drug-development model is a clear mismatch for Meng’s healthcare thesis.
red_flags: Biopharma therapeutics are outside the fund’s stated focus on capex-light Health Tech and Healthcare Services.
No revenue path independent of IND-enabling work, clinical development, or regulatory progress is identified.
Preclinical findings are company-reported; no human clinical evidence is established.
For-profit status, valuation, and proposed financing terms are not established.
unknowns: Legal for-profit status and post-money valuation.
Patent position, freedom to operate, and independent validation of the platform and animal-model findings.
Target indications, patient populations, and evidence supporting the proposed aging-related applications.
Development budget, future capital needs, partnering or licensing strategy, and any near-term revenue plan.
diligence_questions: What is the company’s patent and freedom-to-operate position, and what independent data reproduce the in-cell and animal-model results across relevant mutations and tissues?
What is the lead indication and development plan, including the evidence and regulatory milestones required to reach human trials, and how will the company fund those milestones?
Is there a credible licensing, partnership, or other revenue path before clinical clearance, and what are the company’s for-profit status, valuation, and proposed SAFE or preferred terms?
